title: 半導体工学基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Semiconductor Physics
teachers:
IKENAGA Noriaki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This course provides the foundational knowledge of semiconductors, which underpin all modern technological domains. Specifically, students gain an understanding of crystal structures, classical electron conduction models, the fundamentals of quantum mechanics, energy band theory, and semiconductor material properties from a microscopic perspective at the atomic and molecular level. Additionally, students learn the fundamentals of semiconductor manufacturing processes, such as high-purity crystal growth and photolithography.
advice:
In this course, you will learn the following topics:
(1) History and social context of semiconductor devices (Introduction)
(2) High-purity crystal growth and semiconductor device fabrication processes
(3) Crystal structure
(4) Classical electronic conduction models
(5) Fundamentals of quantum mechanics
(6) Energy band theory in solids
(7) Semiconductor properties and fundamentals of semiconductor devices
Regarding (1) and (2), we may utilize generative AI to investigate the latest information.
requiredKnowledge: Many students may find this subject somewhat more challenging compared to others. This is likely because you will be studying an entirely new branch of physics (quantum mechanics) that you have not encountered before. However, as you progress in understanding the “Fundamentals of Quantum Phenomena”;which reveal the essence of things;you will likely find it a truly fascinating subject. The key to studying this subject is to have a solid grasp of the physics (classical physics) and mathematics you have learned so far.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the role, physical properties, and fundamentals of semiconductor devices.
Be able to explain bonding forces and representative crystal structures.
The motion of electrons can be explained using the Drude theory, mobility, relaxation time, effective mass.
Understand the fundamentals of quantum mechanics and be able to apply the Schrodinger wave equation in practice.
Changes in energy levels of atoms, molecules, and crystalline states, and the formation of energy bands.
Using energy band theory, one can explain the differences between conductors, semiconductors, and insulators.

achievementLevels.ideal:
① Can explain the role and importance of semiconductor devices from multifaceted perspectives.
② Can explain representative crystal structures.
③ Can explain the Schrodinger wave equation by understanding the fundamentals of quantum mechanics.
④ Can derive the energy band structure of solids and use this to explain the differences between conductors, semiconductors, and insulators.
⑤ Can quantitatively explain the electronic properties of semiconductors and device operation using energy band theory.
achievementLevels.standard:
① Can explain the role and importance of semiconductor devices.
② Can explain representative crystal structures.
③ Understands the fundamentals of quantum mechanics and can explain the Schrodinger wave equation, as well as describe results from various applications.
④ Can explain the energy band structure of solids and use it to explain electrical conduction in solids and the differences between conductors, semiconductors, and insulators.
⑤ Can explain the electronic properties of semiconductors and device operation using band theory.

lessons.content:
As an introduction to semiconductor devices,
we will learn about the history of semiconductor
s and the social context surrounding them.

Learn the fundamentals of semiconductor device m
anufacturing processes (high-purity crystal grow
th, film deposition, photolithography, ion impla
ntation, cutting-edge technologies, etc.).

Study the bonding forces in crystals (ionic bond
ing, covalent bonding, metallic bonding)
and representative crystal structures.
Study classical electron conduction models (the
movement of electrons within solids).

Learn the fundamentals of quantum mechanics (par
ticle-wave duality, the uncertainty principle, t
he Schrodinger wave equation, etc.).

Learn the fundamentals of quantum mechanics (inc
luding examples of the application of the Schr&#
246;dinger wave equation, such as the well-type
potential).

Learn the fundamentals of quantum mechanics (hyd
rogen atom, quantum numbers, Pauli exclusion pri
nciple, electron orbitals, electron configuratio
n, etc.).

＜Midterm Review, Comprehensive Exercise＞
Check understanding of material covered in Lesso
ns 1–6 (including short tests)

Study the energy band theory of solids (includin
g the free electron model of metals, the Fermi-D
irac distribution, the electron density distribu
tion in metals, and the Fermi level).

Study solid-state energy band theory (such as th
e Kronig-Penny model).

Study the energy band theory of solids (electron
 motion within crystals, energy band structures
of metals, semiconductors, and insulators, etc.)
.

Learn the fundamentals of semiconductor properti
es (intrinsic semiconductors, n-type semiconduct
ors, p-type semiconductors, etc.).

Learn the fundamentals of semiconductor properti
es (such as the Hall effect).
Learn the fundamentals of semiconductor devices
(such as diodes).

Learn the fundamentals of semiconductor devices
(such as transistors).

Check understanding of previous lessons (includi
ng achievement tests).
